claims.text: The as-cast, homogenized CoCrFeMnNi alloy is a single-phase FCC solid solution.
Homogenization ensures a uniform solid solution in the CoCrFeMnNi alloy.
Prolonged thermal exposure around 600°C induces short-range chemical ordering in CoCrFeMnNi.
Aging at 600°C can induce short-range ordering without forming secondary phases.
The aging-induced short-range order takes the form of nanoscale ordered domains within the FCC matrix.
The proposed ordered domains can be detected and quantified using diffraction, high-resolution TEM, and atom-probe tomography.
Short-range chemical ordering increases local lattice distortion.
The increased local lattice distortion hinders dislocation glide.
Hindered dislocation glide produces localized stress concentrations and early crack initiation.
Early crack initiation caused by ordering reduces fracture toughness and facilitates brittle fracture.
Thermally aged CoCrFeMnNi samples will have lower toughness than the unaged baseline.
Thermally aged CoCrFeMnNi samples will transition from ductile to brittle fracture behavior.
Short-range ordered regions will correlate spatially with crack-initiation sites.
The unaged, homogenized CoCrFeMnNi baseline exhibits uniform dislocation motion and ductile fracture.
The proposed behavior applies to prolonged exposure near 600°C followed by or combined with ambient-temperature mechanical loading.
The ordering and embrittlement effects may differ at substantially different temperatures or loading rates.
Local compositional variation and grain orientation may influence the effect of short-range order on mobility and toughness.
Fracture toughness can be obtained from the proposed standardized tensile tests.

contradictions.description: The baseline is repeatedly called 'as-cast' while also being described as homogenized or solution-treated. An as-cast condition and a post-casting homogenized/solution-treated condition are distinct processing states, so the control state is not defined consistently.
